I’m 54 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time. I can’t chase every new idea. What I do is look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can safely put out. Cotton is still my main crop because I know it well and the land suits it, but I’ll keep some sunflower too. That way, if cotton price is not good or pests get bad, I still have another crop to bring in. With only 2 people at home and some off-farm work, I also can’t make the plan too labor-heavy. So I’ll keep things steady, use well water when the crop really needs it, and not spend too much all at once.

For cotton, I’ll put most of the land there, about 52 mu. I’ll sow in mid to late April, about when the soil warms up well. I usually buy local hybrid seed that people nearby also use. I don’t dare cut fertilizer too much on cotton, because if it grows weak early, it’s hard to recover. But I also won’t push too hard, because fertilizer and water both cost money. So I’ll put a base dressing first, then one or two more applications if the plants look like they need it. I’ll irrigate a couple of times with the well, mainly after planting if it’s dry and again around flowering and boll setting. Cotton needs more watching for insects, so I’ll keep some pesticide ready, mostly for bollworm and aphids, and I’ll spray herbicide once early to save labor.

For sunflower, I’ll keep 20 mu. It doesn’t need as much work as cotton, and it spreads my risk. Around here, if sunflower grows evenly and catches a few good rains, it can still give decent money without too much input. I’ll sow in late April to early May. I won’t spend as much fertilizer on it as cotton. Just enough base fertilizer, maybe one light topdress if the stand looks pale. If rain is short, I can give one or two irrigations from the well, but I won’t overdo it. Sunflower is simpler for this household because we don’t have much spare labor.
